known_stale.why: Nothing in this repository re-pins these two files any more. The hand-rolled re-pinner was `tools/sync.sh`, which has been deleted: it read from a laptop directory that does not exist (`$HOME/Projects/agency/names`) and named a source repository that does not exist (`alphaville-agency/capability`, which 404s). `tools/check-drift.sh` can only RE-VERIFY a pin; it never refreshes one.
known_stale.what_it_means: The hashes above are of the copy this repository carries, so they still prove the copy has not been hand-edited. They do NOT claim the copy is current. The canonical `alphaville-agency/agency/names/` has moved on: upstream is now schema `alphaville.resource-names.v1` while this copy is `v2`, and they differ substantially - upstream has no `claims`, `vocabularies`, `singletons`, `uniqueness` or `exceptions` sections and no `infrastructure` system term, and its `validate.py` is a CLI for rendering and checking names rather than the claims auditor this copy carries. Which of the two is the intended canonical is a decision for the operator; it is NOT assumed here.
known_stale.how_to_refresh: Copy `names/registry.json` and `names/validate.py` from `alphaville-agency/agency` at a chosen commit into `.dsh/ontology/`, write their sha256 into `files` above, set `pinned_at`, and clear this block. There is no script for it: it is a deliberate, reviewed copy of two files, which is cheaper to do by hand than to automate.

rule: This is a derived, read-only copy of the canonical registry in `alphaville-agency/agency` under `names/`. Edit the canonical copy there and re-copy; a local edit here is drift and `tools/check-drift.sh` will fail. `Check-drift.sh` verifies the pin recorded above, and classifies a mismatch against `CANONICAL_NAMES_DIR` when that directory is reachable.
